html:
Tonight I tried to take advantage of an unexpectedly starry sky to redo the collimation of my telescope. I added Bob's knobs (Bob's Knobs) to the secondary mirror to make the process easier.

I had to wait a good hour for the LX90 to reach temperature, and I think it was still too warm. The outside temperature was -14 celsius.

I followed, from memory, the instructions from Thierry Legault. I got to the second step, but the turbulence was too strong to see anything. On top of that, the mill's fog rolled in at the same time. Anyway, sky conditions weren't very good.

I'll have to continue this operation next time.
